title: Baron: instrumental act is fiducia of pardon to be obtained — not already obtained
source_text: LXI. Articulo tamen vigesimo ejusdem Exercitationis cui titulus est, Utrum objectum fidei salvificae sit remissio peccatorum jam impetrata? An vero sit remissio peccatorum impetranda & obtinenda? affirmat & multis argumentis probat, Actum fidei salvificae, qui est causa instrumentalis justificationis, non esse fiduciam veniae, aut remissionis peccatorum impetratae; sed fiduciam veniae impetrandae. Nam, inquit, inter alia, Quicunque Deum orat, ut ei peccata remittat, confidens se esse unum ex eorum numero pro quibus Christus est mortuus; Deumque audientem ejus preces propter Christum, is proculdubio remissionem peccatorum consequitur. Nulla igitur necessitas nos cogit asserere actum fidei salvificae, qui est causa instrumentalis justificationis, esse fiduciam veniae impetratae.
pass_a_gloss: Yet in the twentieth Article of the same Exercise, titled Whether the object of saving faith is remission of sins already obtained? Or rather is remission of sins to be obtained and gotten? he affirms and proves by many arguments that the act of saving faith which is the instrumental cause of justification is not trust of pardon, or of remission of sins obtained; but trust of pardon to be obtained. For, he says, among other things, Whoever prays God that He remit his sins, trusting that he is one of the number for whom Christ died, and that God hears his prayers for Christ, he without doubt obtains remission of sins. Therefore no necessity compels us to assert that the act of saving faith which is the instrumental cause of justification is trust of pardon already obtained.
pass_b_english: Baron art. 20: object — remitted already, or to be obtained?
Instrumental justifying act = fiducia of pardon to be obtained — not of pardon already gotten.
One who prays for remission, trusting he is among those for whom Christ died, obtains remission.
No need to make already-obtained-pardon fiducia the instrumental cause.
